title: How the Python SDK turns ID lists into nested ZPA objects

prose.text: ZPA wrappers accept flat ID lists and rebuild them into the nested `{"id": ...}` lists the API takes.

checks.do: Whether an ID list argument was passed empty or as an already nested list, and which helper handles it.
Which snake_case argument name maps to which wire key for the resource.

transform-helper.statement: `transform_common_id_fields` pops each snake_case key from the source dict and stores a list of `{"id": ...}` objects under the wire key; items that are already dicts with an id are kept.

quotes: id_groups: list, source_dict: dict, target_dict: dict, coerce_ids: bool = True

no-coerce.statement: With `coerce_ids=False` the helper passes ID values through verbatim, which its docstring says ZPA needs because its 19-digit string IDs must be preserved on the wire; `add_segment` in `application_segment.py` calls it that way. The server-group wrapper also calls it that way, but its own loops pop `server_ids` and `app_connector_group_ids` first, so the call changes nothing there and a None for either key still raises TypeError.
no-coerce.conditions: Evidence moved from server_groups.py, where the call is a no-op, to application_segment.add_segment. The v1.11.1 fix for None ID lists (#575) covered application segments only. Previously "With `coerce_ids=False` the helper passes ID values through verbatim, which its docstring says ZPA needs because its 19-digit string IDs must be preserved on the wire; the ZPA server-group wrapper calls it that way."

add-id-groups-truthy.statement: `add_id_groups` reformats an entry only when the keyword value is truthy, so an empty list is left in the keyword arguments under its snake_case name. It is still called by `add_segment_provision` in `application_segment.py`, which also keeps its own `serverGroups` loop, the loop v1.11.1 removed from `add_segment` and `update_segment` (#575), and by the PRA credential pool add and update.
add-id-groups-truthy.conditions: Corrected from "still import" to the callers. add_segment_provision is unchanged between v1.10.0 and HEAD; only add_segment and update_segment lost their loop in v1.11.1. Previously "`add_id_groups` reformats an entry only when the keyword value is truthy, so an empty list is left in the keyword arguments under its snake_case name; `application_segment.py` and `pra_credential_pool.py` still import it."

quotes: body["serverGroups"] = [{"id": group_id} for group_id in body.pop("server_group_ids")]
Fixed ZPA application segment add/update functions raising `TypeError` when `server_group_ids=None` is passed; `None` is now treated as not supplied.
body["serverGroups"] = [{"id": group_id} for group_id in body.pop("server_group_ids")]
body["serverGroups"] = [{"id": group_id} for group_id in body.pop("server_group_ids")]
no longer have a manual `server_group_ids` block in their add/update paths — the helper handles it, which also makes `server_group_ids=None` a no-op instead of a `TypeError` (#575)
`add_segment_provision` keeps its block because it still uses `add_id_groups`.

server-group-keys.statement: The server group wrapper maps `server_ids` to `servers` and `app_connector_group_ids` to `appConnectorGroups`.

segment-keys.statement: The Browser Access segment wrapper lists `clientless_app_ids` to `clientlessApps` and `server_group_ids` to `serverGroups` in its key map, but `add_segment_ba` and `update_segment_ba` take `clientless_app_ids` out before calling transform_common_id_fields: add renames it to `clientlessApps` as given, and update rebuilds it from a BROWSER_ACCESS segment lookup matched by domain, so clientless apps are never rebuilt into `{"id": ...}` objects. Since v1.11.1 `server_group_ids` is mapped only by transform_common_id_fields; up to v1.10.0 each method first built `serverGroups` in its own loop.
segment-keys.conditions: Changed upstream in v1.11.1 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "The Browser Access segment wrapper maps `clientless_app_ids` to `clientlessApps` and `server_group_ids` to `serverGroups`." The clientless_app_ids clause was also corrected: neither method lets transform_common_id_fields see that key, at either pin.
